answer: Before an agent can influence a shared decision, require it to lock a scarce, slashable deposit and earn influence gradually through verified task history. If several new identities try to overwhelm the vote, each must fund its own deposit; identities that coordinate or fail audits lose stake, while newcomers gain little weight. The rule does not prove one person owns one agent, but makes a Sybil swarm costly to create and maintain. Even on an island or in the tundra, a raven’s many aliases cannot multiply locked capital.
